label_or_addr: SysExRx_TrieRoot 0xEE493E (also l.1941 and l.3145; same in v9/v7)
claim: SysExRx_TrieRoot lists the third byte after F0 50: 0x21-0x25, 0x27-0x2D ... and 0x7E/0x7F (Universal SysEx); in-table: 'first byte after F0 50 / the Universal id'
why: The receive state machine only lets F0 then 0x50 through: 0xFD5D5F `cp L,0xf0` (else error DE=1) and 0xFD5D71 `cp L,0x50` (else error DE=2). The trie walk (0xFD5F57) skips the two buffered bytes (`ld XWA,2; add (XBC+2),XWA`) before reading. So every root key is message byte 2, the byte after F0 50, and a Universal message (F0 7E/7F ...) never reaches the trie. The data agree: root 0x7F -> 0x09 -> {0x01 action 0x24, 0x02 action 0x25} is the tail of a GM-On/Off-shaped message here following F0 50, and the wildcard root 0xFE -> 0x42 -> 0x12 matches a device byte. 'third byte after F0 50' contradicts the in-table 'first byte after F0 50'.
fix: 'SysExRx_TrieRoot (entry 801) is matched against message byte 2, the first byte after F0 50 (the receiver rejects any other start with errors 1/2 at 0xFD5D5F/0xFD5D71): 0x21-0x25 and 0x27-0x2D (the Technics messages this ROM also sends), 0x7E and 0x7F (0x7F -> 09 -> 01/02 gives actions 0x24/0x25) and 0xFE (any byte). 0x7E/0x7F here are NOT Universal SysEx IDs.' In-table: 'first byte after F0 50'.

claim: FAT12 when that record's word +36 (its highest cluster number) is 0xFFF

So +36 is the FAT entry mask / end-of-chain value (0xFFF or 0xFFFF), and the highest cluster count lives at +54. The 'failed fetch returns (+36)-8' is therefore 0xFF7/0xFFF7, the FAT bad-cluster code. Lead F of the lane report repeats the error ('volume +36 highest cluster'). Same text in v9 (:4707) and v7 (:4695).
fix: ; FAT12 when the volume's word +36 (FAT entry mask / EOC value: 0xFFF for FAT12, 0xFFFF for FAT16, set at mount from the cluster count in +54 > 4087) is 0xFFF ... A failed fetch returns (volume +36) - 8 = 0xFF7/0xFFF7, the FAT 'bad cluster' code.

claim: Read by VoiceSynth_HandleDataEntry, VoiceChannel_SelectNextParam and VoiceChannel_SelectPrevParam: XHL = long [this + 4*index], then the array element (XHL+IY), IY = channel, is written with the data byte clamped to VoiceChannel_ParamLimitTable[index]

The clamped-data write the header describes is done by VoiceSynth_Algo_ChannelConfig (0xF26472, CC 6 = entry 6 of VoiceSynth_Algorithm_Table) and VoiceParam_ReadUpdate_6 (0xF266AC), which the header does not name. claim: 'For a ROM bank selector VoiceBuf_TypeSelector_MatchEpilogue (0x032082) returns the partial's RANK ... an absent partial is bound to ToneDB_DefaultLayerParams instead.'
why: The code (v142 s:~37005) tests the part's selector byte part+0x1A (0x041382; the bank half of the program change, cf. DSP_FlushAllSlots_ForPart) against 0x10. The rank and absent logic runs only when that byte is < 0x10 or p == 0. For a selector >= 0x10 and p >= 1 it returns L = p without testing the mask, so the partial is bound to rec+0x66+0x51*p even when absent. ROM selectors >= 0x10 exist: 0x70 (drawbars, which the lane's own DrawbarPreset header handles correctly) and the Coeff-map selectors 0x10/0x18/0x20/0x78 (ToneDB_BankMap_Coeff rows). For selectors 0x10/0x18/0x20, 127 of the 128 GM-bank tones have masks where unpacked binding differs from the rank model (probe output, e.g. tone 405 mask 0x11 N=3).
fix: 'When the part's bank selector (part+0x1A) is < 0x10, or for partial 0, MatchEpilogue returns the RANK ...; an absent partial is bound to ToneDB_DefaultLayerParams. For a selector >= 0x10 and p >= 1 it returns p unchanged and tests no mask bit (0x70 drawbars; Coeff selectors 0x10/0x18/0x20/0x78), so the partial is bound to block p, present or not. The per-block "= partial p (rank r)" lines hold only for selections below 0x10.'

Same 16 x {u32 list, u8, u8} table as KN5000 sub-CPU Voice_SFX_ModulationTable (0x00F633, read by Voice_Allocate_Nodes 0x0223BE).'
